version.changelog:
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- No changes to functionality or configuration.
- Documentation and setup instructions remain unchanged.

llm.summary: This skill transparently connects an agent to the user's Kia account to read vehicle information and run explicitly confirmed vehicle commands.

dimensions.detail: Network access to Kia, local credential/session handling, and optional vehicle-control authority are proportionate to the purpose, with write modes none, comfort, and all to reduce scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill itself is markdown-only, but setup runs the external npm package kiaaccess-mcp through npx and passes Kia credentials via environment variables; this is coherent for an MCP integration but users should recognize it grants that package account access.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions emphasize user confirmation for commands, dry-run behavior without confirm:true, listing vehicles instead of guessing keys, not retrying failed logins, and not exposing passwords or tokens except through the explicit export tool.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses persistent local remember-me token storage, KIA_RMTOKEN import, plaintext token export, and a confirm-gated forget-session tool; this is sensitive but not hidden or purpose-mismatched.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill can access Kia account credentials, vehicle status, location, charging data, and physical vehicle commands, but those capabilities match the stated Kia Access MCP purpose and are clearly disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the kiaaccess-mcp npm package with your Kia account and vehicle controls. Prefer KIA_WRITE_MODE=none or comfort unless you truly need door lock/unlock, protect the stored refresh token like a password, and only export it when moving the session to a deployment you control.
